sections.en: CBOE Volatility Index is changing hands near $14.90, +0.61% over the past 24 hours and -16.48% on a 7-day view. Spot trades below the 50-day average ($16.13) and below the 200-day average ($17.60), keeping the medium-term structure defensive. The 30-day tape reads as a consolidation phase (-3.62%), suggesting the market is still rotating within a range.

**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is fully inverted (price < EMA20 < EMA50 < EMA200), the classic bear-stack in which rallies into value tend to be sold. Spot at $14.90 versus EMA20 $15.84, EMA50 $16.13 and EMA200 $17.60 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $14.89 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $13.52 as the 2σ downside envelope; first resistance at $14.92 (recent swing high); upper band $17.80 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $1.369 implies a typical daily range of roughly 9.2 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 45.6 — neutral territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits below its signal line (0.008305 vs 0.06027, histogram -0.05196), consistent with fading momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 108%; the 20-day band spans 27% of the mid — expanded, which favors trend continuation tactics. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned -3.62% over 30 days and -13.67% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (-16.48%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires acceptance above $14.92 on expanding turnover. Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $14.89; failed reclaims of the 50-day average ($16.13). In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on CBOE Volatility Index: spot $14.90 with the medium-term bias defensive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (+0.61%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
